title: Synthesizers
subtitle: How a sound is built
summary: Why a clarinet and a flute sound different on the same note, and how a synthesizer builds both from bare waves. The first half works through the physics of sound and the parts of a signal chain: harmonics, filters that shape vowels, envelopes, FM bells, distorted guitar chords and echo. The second half maps those ideas onto the controls of a real instrument, from modulation matrices and step sequencers to the TB-303 bass line, ending with five sounds built from a blank patch. Branches cover reverb, wavetables, Hammond drawbars, Homer Dudley's vocoder and granular synthesis.

release.note: A copy edit by a second reader: clearer sentences, facts checked, and a few new footnotes.
